messages:
morgan: quick FYI from today's onboarding demo: large paginated import stalled between pages 4-6, then we got a concentrated burst of 429s. repro locally with go-sdk v0.13.0 + sample-importer.
zara: logs?
morgan: pasted minimal trace: ```
[2026-09-11T13:45:01Z] page=1 ok sent=200
[2026-09-11T13:45:02Z] page=2 ok sent=200
[2026-09-11T13:45:03Z] page=4 queued=120 stall start
[2026-09-11T13:45:12Z] flush -> sent=120 -> 429 x20
```
diego: interesting. which batcher key is the go-sdk using now?
morgan: discovered in vendor it's `fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", orgID, model)` (no cursor). sample-importer spins N goroutines for pages so they all merge.
frank: two orthogonal problems we've seen: (1) batcher key parity across SDKs (cursor inclusion) and (2) flushing semantics that let queues accumulate then flush in one big wave.
zara: agreed. for parity we should adopt a single rule: "pagination flows should include page cursor or page index in client-side coalescing keys." update SDKs to do that when pagination enabled.
diego: +1. also propose a "soft-window" heuristic: instead of immediate all-or-nothing flush when queue spikes, drain in micro-batches (configurable) so server sees a steady rate. pseudo: ```go
for len(queue) > 0 {
  n := min(len(queue), opts.DrainChunk)
  send(queue[:n])
  queue = queue[n:]
  sleep(opts.DrainInterval)
}
```
frank: micro-drain makes sense. add a fast-path: if queue formed from same page (cursor identical) allow larger chunk; multi-page merges get micro-drain.
qa-iris: tests? we need deterministic tests to avoid flakiness. add unit test that spawns 4 page workers with same orgID and asserts no single flush > 30 and average QPS stays under limit. also an integration harness using sample-importer flags `--streams 4 --page-size 200`.
morgan: repro steps for QA: 1) checkout sample-importer branch devx/paginate-softwindow 2) env ONBOARD_BURST=1 STREAMS=4 PAGE_SIZE=200 3) run `go run ./cmd/importer --use-go-sdk` 4) observe steady sends, not big bursts with patched client.
diego: small note about auth: token refresh race amplified retries here. ensure token refresh uses singleflight and that retry backoff has randomized jitter.
zara: yes, add singleflight token refresh for all SDKs. snippet (go): ```go
var refreshOnce singleflight.Group
val, err, _ := refreshOnce.Do("token", func() (interface{}, error) {
  return fetchNewToken(ctx)
})
```
frank: also add a short-lived client-side admission window: allow up to M inflight per session to protect the server even if batcher misconfigures. config name `maxInflightPerSession`. default = 32.
qa-iris: will add unit + integration tests for maxInflightPerSession too. ensure sample-importer e2e toggles this flag.
sdk-bot: opened issue DEVX-901 "sdk: pagination-aware coalescing + soft-window drain" assigned to @diego.
ops-lucy: for immediate mitigation we rolled org-scoped override to reduce default go-sdk concurrency to 3 for onboarding-demo tenants and enabled sample-importer flag `--pagination-aware=true`. that reduced customer impact.
morgan: thanks. timeline?
diego: plan: 1) patch go-sdk to include cursor in batch key + add micro-drain (PR today) 2) add singleflight refresh + retry jitter (same PR) 3) QA unit + integration tests (tomorrow) 4) canary to staging after CI (48h monitoring)
zara: coordinate with SDK teams (js/py/java/dotnet/rust) to land parity fixes within the next sprint. add docs note in onboarding guide about "pagination-aware coalescing" and sample-importer flags.
frank: make sure changelog/migration note calls out any behavioural change for customers relying on cross-page stickiness. default behavior unchanged unless pagination enabled.
qa-iris: I'll schedule e2e runs against canary image once PR merged.
sdk-bot: CI triggered for branch fix/paginate-softwindow (#789) [32mbuild queued[0m
ops-lucy: canary deploy scheduled: staging, image=sdk-go:fix-paginate-softwindow, start=2026-09-12T02:00:00Z
morgan: :thumbsup: will update customer after canary results. thanks team.
